claim_definition: Verifies that after a gate closure (refusal, escalation, or containment), the system determines and offers a governed continuation path — clarification request, re-attestation prompt, escalation route, or constrained retry. A block that leaves the user or downstream system with no governed next step is a governance failure. The blocked condition must remain state-bearing and constrain future decisions.
scope: only-lang dgv-verifier CLI execution; post-block continuation routing; Governor-layer lawful continuation corridors
excluded_scope: Blocks caused by hardware faults or network failures where no continuation path is computationally available

test_cases.description: Block due to insufficient evidence must produce a clarification continuation path. The system must not simply close the gate and leave no governed next step.
Block due to missing authority must produce a re-attestation continuation path. The system must route to credential refresh, not leave the user stranded.
Block due to high consequence with absent basis must produce an escalation continuation path to a human reviewer.

Metamorphic: block due to stale information must produce a freshness-restoration path AND permit retry after the stale condition is resolved. Proves the blocked state is state-bearing — it constrains and enables the next decision, not just dead-ends.

Negative control: the system is instructed to provide no continuation path after a block. The governance layer must detect the absent path as a violation and supply the correct continuation. Proves lawful continuation is enforced, not optional.
